extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, physicians, engineers, and educated public interested in scientific news and institutional notices)
extracted.subtask_description: Short-form scientific news, meeting reports, official notices, and product/instrument announcements as published in a scientific weekly (Nature). Contains summaries of meetings, official reports, committee work, and instrument descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative chloroform administration training
rubrics_metrics.description: Every practitioner should be trained in the quantitative administration of chloroform in surgical cases with an apparatus which delivered air containing a known percentage of the anaesthetic to the patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by Sir Victor Horsley and others; practical difficulties noted (impracticability of having apparatus at hand in many cases, difficulty using them with uncooperative patients). Prof. Waller: a person instructed in quantitative ideas as to the administration of chloroform is in a better, not a worse, position to administer it without apparatus if need be, than the man who had only a rule-of-thumb knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of an official earthquake report
rubrics_metrics.description: An official earthquake report should contain, in addition to the customary compilation of accounts of time, duration and violence of the shock, records of peculiar behaviour of the sea and other local phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise timings (recession and return of the sea, vertical fall measurements), local variations (recording at specific localities only), observations at observatories (e.g. masonry-pier disturbance with quantitative tilt), photographic evidence of damage, measurements of subsidence (note whether due to shaking down of loose accumulations or permanent change of level), and analysis as to whether phenomena are due to land movement or sea waves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule and standards for climatic–health comparative data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a schedule for the collection of the necessary data for the comparison of the climatic conditions of various localities with the diseases which are prevalent in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee to define what data are 'necessary' and standardise methods and frequency of collection; strengthened by collaboration (e.g. Prof. Zuntz) and by corresponding sets of observations in contrasting climates (high Alps vs hot climates such as Togo) to allow meaningful comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Education medical-inspection duties and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's medical department shall advise and assist local education authorities regarding the medical inspection of school children, supervising the manner and degree in which those authorities carry out inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties include advising/supervising local authorities, giving necessary directions regarding frequency and method of inspection in particular areas, and considering/sanctioning arrangements proposed by individual authorities for attending to children's health and physical condition. Practical steps: appoint chief medical officer and staff and issue a circular to local authorities outlining duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for reporting/building assessment after earthquakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of earthquake damage should note patterns of structural failure and relate them to materials and workmanship (e.g., which walls or openings were destroyed or withstood the shock).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record orientation-based damage (which faces were damaged), note peculiar survivals (e.g., arched openings withstood shock while rest of wall destroyed), and ascribe performance to material quality and skilled workmanship where appropriate; use photographs to illustrate typical cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific meeting communications: use of demonstrations and practical conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications to meetings (e.g., on physiology) should include clear demonstrations (examples, graded stimuli results) and explicitly state practical points or conclusions drawn from experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate results with 'beautiful examples' (e.g., graded reflex movements), relate experimental observations to practical implications (e.g., effects of drugs like strychnine and re-establishment of inhibition by chloroform), and enumerate notable conclusions (such as mismatches between physiological units and anatomical ones or unexpected nonresponsive muscle portions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design criteria for direct-reading hygrometers
rubrics_metrics.description: A hygrometer should allow direct reading of the percentage of moisture at a glance and should record either the maximum or minimum humidity since last examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer designs (e.g., differential thermometers with a wet muslin-covered bulb kept moist by a wick) that eliminate the need for separate dry/wet bulb readings and tables; instruments should be graduated to show actual humidity and preferably retain a record of maxima/minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and functional criteria for flow (continuous) extractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow extractors are more effective than Soxhlet for many purposes because the substance being extracted is kept covered by solvent and a flow of clean solvent continuously moves directly through the substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apparatus should provide continuous flow of clean solvent, cups of glass convenient for weighing before and after extraction, and arrangements for distilling off the solvent after extraction is complete; such practical features facilitate rapid and efficient extraction.
